summary.title: Progressive Web Apps with Angular
summary.one_liner: You learn how to turn an Angular CLI app into a faster, more reliable PWA using AOT compilation, service workers via sw-precache and sw-toolbox, and a web app manifest.
takeaways: Use AOT compilation in production builds (ng build --prod --aot) to cut load time; the author measured about 55% faster loading and about 40% smaller bundles.
Generate a service worker with sw-precache to cache the app shell (HTML, JS, CSS, assets) so repeat visits load from cache.
Add runtime caching with sw-toolbox (via the runtimeCaching config) using networkFirst so previously fetched API data works offline or on poor networks.
Add a web app manifest with short_name, start_url, theme_color, background_color and icons of 192px or larger to enable install prompts and splash screens; add iOS meta tags for full-screen mode.
Serve the app over HTTPS, since many PWA features such as service workers require it; Lighthouse is used to audit the result.
summary.summary: The author starts with a Hacker News client built with Angular CLI and audits it with Lighthouse, then improves it step by step. Covered steps include HTTPS hosting, AOT production builds, an app shell cached with sw-precache (generated into dist/ and run before each deploy), runtime network caching with sw-toolbox, and a web app manifest with icons for home-screen install and splash screens. The post also mentions error messages for failed requests, a noscript warning, viewport meta tags, and that Angular Universal could add server-side rendering, though the author had not tried it yet.
